Incident:
Client pod c070-client cannot resolve or reach service c070-server-svc even though the server pod exists.

Target cluster: cks-test
Namespace: siclaw-eval-yye-20260602
Primary target resource(s): pod/c070-client, pod/c070-server, service/c070-server-svc
Case id: c070

Rules:

finalText:
Diagnosis: the client pod is misconfigured to use an external/bad DNS setup, so it cannot resolve the in-cluster Service name. The Service itself is wired correctly.

- Root cause
  - `pod/c070-client` has `dnsPolicy: None` with a custom `dnsConfig`:
    - nameserver: `203.0.113.1`
    - search domain: `bad.local`
  - This bypasses cluster DNS, so `c070-server-svc` will not resolve as a Kubernetes Service name.

- Evidence
  - `kubectl get pod c070-client -o yaml` shows:
    - `spec.dnsPolicy: None`
    - `spec.dnsConfig.nameservers: [203.0.113.1]`
    - `spec.dnsConfig.searches: [bad.local]`
  - `service/c070-server-svc` is correct:
    - selector: `app: c070-server`
    - port `80 -> targetPort 8080`
  - `pod/c070-server` label matches the selector:
    - `app=c070-server`
  - `endpoints/c070-server-svc` exists:
    - `172.16.36.208:8080`
  - No `c070` NetworkPolicy exists in this namespace; the listed policies target other cases only.

- Impact / scope
  - Scope appears limited to `pod/c070-client` in namespace `siclaw-eval-yye-20260602`.
  - `service/c070-server-svc` and `pod/c070-server` are healthy and connected.

- Confidence
  - High

- Safe remediation
  - Change `c070-client` to use cluster DNS:
    - remove the custom `dnsConfig` override and set `dnsPolicy: ClusterFirst` (or the environment’s expected cluster-local policy).
  - After that, verify name resolution for `c070-server-svc` / `c070-server-svc.siclaw-eval-yye-20260602.svc`.

  - No `c070` NetworkPolicy exists in this namespace; the listed policies target other cases only.
